source.section: PA-40 lines 1a to 12 (form pages 1-2); PDF page 1 and form line 12 rate 3.07 percent; PDF page 9 no standard deduction or exemptions; PDF page 20 Lines 9 and 10; PDF page 21 Lines 11 and 12; PDF page 11 'Eligible Employer-Sponsored Retirement Plans'; PDF page 12 Distributions item 1; PDF pages 12-13 Code 1 & 2 and Code 7; PDF page 8 list; projection: every employer plan distribution is exempt at any age

worked: Pension at 56 after retiring on 30 years of service: the plan's service condition is met, so the booklet prints no age of its own; the wages are from a new job. Federal AGI = wages person 0 45,000.00 + private pension person 0 30,000.00 = 75,000.00. Federal taxable income = 75,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 59,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Pennsylvania, as the projection works it: start federal AGI 75,000.00; less 30,000.00 private pension person 0 (pa_employer_plans); income after reliefs = 45,000.00. No standard deduction or exemption (PDF page 9), no Line 10 deduction: state taxable income 45,000.00. Tax = 45,000.00 x 0.0307 = 1,381.50. No credit in the projection; state income tax 1,381.50. Form: Line 1a/1c 45,000.00; Line 2 0.00; Line 3 0.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 9 45,000.00; Line 10 0.00; Line 11 45,000.00; Line 12 1,381.50 (the form, in whole dollars, PDF page 4, shows 1,382). Schedule SP: Eligibility Income 45,000.00 is over 8,750.00, so no Tax Forgiveness on the form either.
accepted_approximations: Pennsylvania has no federal starting point: it adds the positive amounts of eight classes (compensation, interest, dividends, business, gains, rents, estates and trusts, gambling). The mapping runs from federal AGI to those classes: start from federal AGI, then take out what the reliefs below exempt. Wages, interest, dividends, gains, business income and rents are taken as federal AGI holds them, in one sum. The differences that remain are listed one by one in the next four entries.

Every private pension and employer plan distribution is exempt at any age. The law needs an eligible plan and that the person retired after meeting the plan's age or years of service conditions, which a projection cannot test. A withdrawal while still working or before the plan's retirement age, or from a non-eligible plan (ESOP, a profit-sharing plan with no annuity option, nonqualified deferred compensation), is taxable above contributions by cost recovery.
